 Order

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.168/2023 registered at Police Station - Hatta, District Balaghat (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in detention since 03.10.2023.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 11.09.2023 the prosecutrix aged about 17 years 04 months 16 days was found missing from the house, therefore, missing report was lodged and police started investigation.

On 02.10.2023, she was recovered along with the applicant and thereafter she was medically examined but no definite opinion was given and x-ray was also conducted in which she was found to be more than 18 years, thereafter her statement has been recorded by the police and in the statement she said that she went to the applicant by train from Balaghat to Gondia then to Vijaywada and resided there with applicant and while residing in Vijaywada, the applicant Rahul Tekam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3841349/
1 committed intercourse with her, therefore, offence has been registered against him under the aforesaid sections.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 03.10.2023.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix was more than 18 years at the time of incident.
The statement of mother of prosecutrix under section 164 of Cr.P.C. has been recorded in which nothing has been stated against the applicant.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. has stated that she herself went to Vijaywada, applicant did not took her.
Applicant was working as a laborer in Vijaywada.
Charge sheet has been filed.
There is no criminal record against the applicant.
Trial of the case will take considerable time to conclude.

Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code o f Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE DPS Rahul Tekam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3841349/
